item.title: Seeking Greenlight- Australia: Seeking Greenlight- Australia
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Geographical/Memetic - A twist on a conspiracy thory
Elevator Pitch: The conspiracy theory that Australia does not exist is, in fact, true and is just a way to contain a memetic contagion, that makes people believe that Australia is a thing.

Central Narrative: Kind of a basic SCP article, which states that the conspiracy theory was an idea to contain and/or stop the spread of this anomaly, but in the end the article states that the Lead Resercher is waiting for the approval to use amnestics all over the world to delete the meme.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think the idea of twisting a (quite) well-known conspiracy, that it is actually true, is interesting.

Additional Notes: I was thinking of putting in a drawn outline of Australia as an "illustration on how people believe the SCP looks like", but I am not sure whether or not that goes against the rules of a memetic agent.

item.title: An atavistic humanoid + a mysterious organization: Re: An atavistic humanoid + a mysterious organization
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the critique! I did pass the 400 word count, but luckily Zyn fixed it for me.

+ Answers and reaction
- close
  • As for your first question: Yes, I intended on having humans in the past have this ability. There are a lot of stories about people with psychic powers, and some claim to posses it this day. The idea was that it was a rare mutation, that occurred in the past. That it wasn't some sort of superpower, but more like an reflex/instinctive reaction. It could for example be triggered by strong emotions. The thing is that those people either died at a young age because of the effects of the mutation, went insane, or got killed by other humans who thought they were dangerous. It wasn't beneficial for them.
  • About the IQ, what you are describing (not mathematically intelligent, but better in things that were useful around that time) is what I meant. Thank you for correcting me.
  • Evolution is (mostly) positive for the survival of the concerning organism's genes, right?
  • Negative in the current environment I meant. I do not think one of our ancestors would go good with today's environment.
  • So….. found remains of one of the ''psychic cavemen''. Are you suggesting that that is a better option?
  • Last but not least: about Latin. I was wondering what language the organization would be speaking, and since it is kind off a cult who wants to bring back ancient creatures trough science I figured that Latin would be fitting. The earliest version of the organization was around the 16th century, at the time of the renaissance (the time period where people were really inspired by the ancient cultures and the time period where almost all of the humanists/scientists wrote their papers in Latin). Wouldn't it make sense for the organization to have Latin as their spoken/taught language?

PS: I just tried to describe my idea in a sentence and ''An organization determined to recreate ancient mythological creatures creates a psychic caveman with trust issues'' doesn't sound as good as it sounded before. So allow me to ask you a question: is the no greenlight a ''you need to improve this idea''-no greenlight or a ''you could better start working on something else''-no greenlight?

item.title: Sir Reginald: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello! Not an official critter here, but I can still read and give opinions.
So, I mostly agree with Grigori above. The idea is really cool, I personally love this kind of 'meta' stuff. But I would also recommend cutting out the anomalous weapon bit. I don't think the possession is a problem myself, it makes sense as a way for a fictional character to 'anchor' itself to our reality; but I think the anomalous weapons bit would simply make it look as though you're making it be more dangerous than it needs to be.
Not everything needs to be able to destroy a plane to be interesting.

This aside, I believe, another interesting concept you could explore instead- if you think the personal woes of Sir Reginald coming to terms with not being "real" are not enough- is how they got here at all, if that is still an active phenomenon/it can spread to other media, and what that means for whatever work Reginald is from originally.
Just a bunch of ideas, you're free to completely disregard them if you don't feel they're interesting enough for you.

Overall though, I really like this! Definitely gonna be reading it once it's written out as a draft and hopefully as a real Object!

item.title: The Normality: Re: The Normality
item.content:encoded:
Hi.
I've read your crit and I wanted to clear some things.
Firstly, I wasn't aware of the Djoric-Dmatix Proposal and its similarity to my idea until now. Thank you for that.
Secondly, while your concern about them being similar are true, I think they are different in essence.
1.) The Djoric-Dmatix Proposal, or the thirty-six, are somewhat aware of what they are capable of, and are part of something huge. However, the normality is just an average person, who lives an average life not knowing what he is and what he could do, and with no part of something grandiose.

2.) The normality does not influence anomalies over a large area, just that which is under his observation or could potentially affect his normal life. This shows that if he was left alone, he would not have affected the foundation or anything at all, and even now, with proper precaution, could be controlled, unlike the thirty-six

3.) The Thirty-Six are contained because they possess a risk of generating large amounts of anomaly upon death, and affecting the entire world. The normality is observed for a different reason, that is, his power to bring equilibrium could wipe out the foundation's existence without actually ending the world, not for threatening reality as we now know it. In other words, the normality is given SCP status not because he is anomalous, but rather because he is normal, a bit too much.

I am sure that you will have more concerns. If so, please do not hesitate to give me your feedback
Thank you

item.title: Any suggestion for my first SCP? Feel free to comment: Re: Any suggestion for my first SCP? Feel free to comment
item.content:encoded:
Hello there, hope you are having a pleasant day. I have checked your SCP and it has mistakes, I will tell you some:
- You cant resign the object class after it breaches containment since the object classes are based on 1. Threat and 2. Percentage of breaching containment. For example, not every safe object class SCP is harmless it just means they are easy to contain.
- You are just talking about the background of the SCPs and not of actual SCPs aka mannequins so the audience can't tell you exactly what you are missing and what you are doing right.
- You should format your article that it's 2m x 2m x 2m meters for example containment since you are containing them in cubes, not flat squares.
- And the last one the description is too short, you barely explain their ability and their looks so that has to be longer.

I wish you a pleasant day and good luck with writing.

item.title: My First SCP Idea: Re: My First SCP Idea
item.content:encoded: Iunno, this doesn't really vibe with me as is. Like, you're really trying to write an interesting short story here: the plane rebuilding and there being a threat of stuff happening if it succeeds isn't an awful idea (though it feels somewhat reminiscent of SCP-682) but it's a base for the story: you're going to have to figure out y'know, what the Foundation do to prevent this and how you can show this challenge in an interesting way to readers; and like, how the challenge can escalate in stakes so that you can reach this final, thrilling conclusion.

item.title: The Spire - needs greenlights: Re: The Spire - needs greenlights
item.content:encoded:
This idea feels…incredibly complex but without paying it off in an interesting way. Like, you have a spire with a tonne of random properties that are all like, kinda related and it might be fine if you did something interesting with it, but you…don't? The like, list of things that can cause a teleportation event in particular feels, complex instead of interesting: my general advice is to strip an anomaly down to the fewest moving parts it needs so you can focus on the interesting bits instead of producing a tonne of rules about how it works.

I think that's my bigger issue to be honest: the discovery section is fine but it feels like something you'd include as a quick nod to how it was found over the meat of the article, and the only other planned thing is 'test logs' but I don't really have a feel for what they actually like…involve?

I guess my top advice here is that you're trying to write an interesting short story, not a cool weird thing to include in a ttrpg; the way the the foundation interacts with this and what happens with it is going to be the key that makes this work.

item.title: What is Love?: Re: What is Love?
item.content:encoded:
The original intent for the story was that I was going to leave it open-ended; the beginning essentially takes real-world recent history and views it through a fantastic lens. The idea was that the stalemate is still ongoing but appears to be losing effectiveness as time progresses (utilizing events such as Japan's birthrate reaching its lowest recorded number last year and America's marriage rates reaching a record low the year before as evidence).

My concern with this is that the open-ended nature here feels unsatisfying: the truce slowly falling apart feels…like a fine progression but I think it'd feel like it was missing closure if we didn't see how it all ended?

I also have some concerns about the progression through this: it feels…perhaps too loose? Like, in the sense that, I don't really have a clear idea of what the in article discussion is as the effectiveness is lost or like, what stance the various members of the stalemate are taking or anything.

Having tales building off this isn't a terrible idea but it feels…perhaps like they might feel stronger if included in the SCP?

item.title: SCP Idea: Re: SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
You're going to have to give someone a lot more detail here before they can tell whether this idea is interesting: remember, you have 400 words to use to explain this.

Hermit crabs that do weird things.

Strange hermit crabs that seem to be connected in an anomalous way

Like, connected in an anomalous way how? What weird things do they do? Why does them having killed people in Naples, Florida matter? What's the actual story you're telling within this SCP?

Despite giving very little detail, this feels kinda reminiscent of SCP-5915 but at the moment, that's only because 'death', 'gulf of mexico' and 'hermit crabs' and it's very possible you're taking this in a completely different direction.

item.title: SCP Idea Seeks Greenlight: Re: SCP Idea Seeks Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for critique
– hide block

Small items may be offered as 'tribute' to prevent the doll's nature from taking important concepts/people.

What do you mean by 'taking' here? Is this like…a semantic hazard which might take the meaning of 'freedom' so no-one understands what it means anymore? Or is this more a small scale thing where it might take the concept of freedom which allows it to be free/to be interpreted as free?

To remain generally inert, the item must receive a tribute every 2-3 days.

I'm, generally not a fan of SCPs that like, force the Foundation to interact with them in this way; it's generally more interesting (at least to me) if they willingly choose to do something because then it opens you up to asking the question 'why did they choose to do this'.

This doll embodies Otaku obsession culture and gatekeeping culture as satire, giving a supernatural explanation for such phenomena.

As a satire, this feels…off? It doesn't so much satirise the phenomenon as just, repeat it verbatim but with a supernatural cause. This isn't necessarily an issue alone though.

The core of my concern with this proposal is that we have this interesting start to the story: the discovery of the anomaly, the identification of the otaku, the thing coming into foundation contact; but I don't know where all these individual parts go: what do you do with them all? How do you explore the idea of obsessive culture and otaku-ness and gatekeeping in this? What conclusions do you draw about it? Where do the interviews and the found footage take this narratively?

I have some concerns about the compulsive nature of this, it feels to me that the doll somehow inspiring the creation of otakus without forcing people to become them would be more interesting: it'd really let you like, explore why some people become so obsessive.
